history.text:
The root of this story is an old puzzle. What should a central bank do when oil, not strong demand, pushes prices up? In the 1970s–80s the Fed mostly avoided raising rates against oil-driven inflation. An analysis by Funcas calls the 1979 Iranian revolution shock the closest precedent to 2026.

The present shock began on 28 February 2026, when US and Israeli strikes on Iran started. In early March the Strait of Hormuz, which carries about a fifth of the world's oil, was effectively shut. Brent crude topped $110 a barrel on 23 March. That month the Fed and the European Central Bank (ECB) held rates but warned about inflation.

The ECB acted first. It became the first major central bank to raise rates over war-driven inflation, in June and again in September, taking its deposit rate to 2.50%. The Fed made its first rise of this cycle in September: a quarter-point, to 3.75–4%. In October India's Reserve Bank (RBI) raised its repo rate to 5.50%, its first rise since February 2023. On 28 October the Fed held, but Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voted for a rise. The Fed's last half-point rise was in December 2022.

lesson.concept: How monthly price rises add up to yearly inflation
lesson.big_idea: Inflation is often reported month by month. Each month's rise builds on the one before, so small monthly numbers pile up. A 0.3% monthly rise is about 3.7% a year.

steps.title: A price index tracks a basket
steps.text: A price index like the CPI tracks the cost of a fixed basket of things people buy: food, fuel, rent, insurance. Each month officials report how much that basket's cost changed.

steps.title: Monthly changes look tiny
steps.text: Monthly numbers are small, like 0.2% or 0.4%. In October US prices rose 0.4%, and core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3%.

steps.title: Rises build on rises
steps.text: Each month's rise applies to a price that is already higher, like interest earning interest. This is called compounding. So to get a yearly figure, you multiply the monthly growth twelve times.

steps.title: Quick rule: times twelve
steps.text: For small numbers, multiplying by 12 gets close: 0.3% × 12 = 3.6%. Compounding nudges it to about 3.7%. That matches the three-month annualised core pace, meaning turned into a yearly rate, reported for October.

steps.title: Why 0.1 point matters
steps.text: At 0.2% a month, prices rise about 2.4% a year; at 0.3%, about 3.7%. So a 0.1-point monthly miss adds up to about 1.3 points a year. Waller named 0.3% as his line for considering a half-point rise.

example.result: A gap of just 0.1 point a month became a gap of about 1.3 points a year: 2.4% versus 3.7%. Small monthly misses add up.

stories.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price range, aiming for up to $1.4 trillion
stories.question: Why is Anthropic seeking a $1.4 trillion valuation, and can markets absorb it?
stories.dek: Anthropic makes the Claude AI models. It wants to sell shares on Nasdaq at $70–$78 each. Its price tag depends on which shares you count, and the sale comes during a shaky time for AI stocks.

so_far.text: Anthropic is the AI company that makes Claude. It has raised money from private investors, who last valued it at $965 billion in May 2026. On 26 October 2026 it published its S-1. That is the document a company files with US regulators before it sells shares to the public. On 27 October Indian IT stocks fell after the filing revived worries about AI. Infosys dropped about 2.3% and TCS about 2.1%.

what_happened.text: On 10 November 2026 Anthropic updated its filing with a price range. It plans to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each on Nasdaq, under the ticker 'ANT'. That could raise up to $64.35 billion, or up to $90.4 billion counting cornerstone investors. Separately, Google, Nvidia and AMD are part of a $26 billion private placement. Reuters, Bloomberg and the New York Times report a target valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. The Wall Street Journal says $1.3 trillion. NBC says the range implies about $1.02 trillion. CNBC reports trading could start around 19 November.

steps.text: Frontier AI needs huge amounts of computing power. Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in compute commitments, which are deals to pay for that power.
Private rounds of $30 billion and $65 billion were already huge. A public listing can reach a far wider pool of buyers.
Investors pay for growth. Third-quarter revenue hit $16.96 billion, up 47% on the quarter before, though growth slowed from 144%.
Valuation is share price times share count. NBC puts it near $1.02 trillion, and $1.4 trillion appears to count all possible future shares.
Whether markets absorb it depends on mood. SpaceX raised $75 billion in June, but an AI-stock selloff has split Wall Street banks.

history.text:
Anthropic was founded in January 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, including Dario and Daniela Amodei. By May 2021 it had raised $124 million, a small sum next to what came later. In March 2023 it launched Claude, so it now had a product to sell. Big backers followed: Amazon began investing in September 2023, and Google in October 2023.

In 2025 the price investors paid rose fast. A March round valued Anthropic at $61.5 billion. In September it raised $13 billion at a $183 billion valuation. In the same year it agreed to pay $1.5 billion to settle a copyright case.

In February 2026 it raised $30 billion at $380 billion. That was more than TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech were worth combined. Around the same time it got into a dispute with the Pentagon, the US defence department, over its limits on surveillance and autonomous weapons. In March the Pentagon labelled Anthropic a supply-chain risk. In May a $65 billion raise valued it at $965 billion.

Next came the move to the stock market. Anthropic filed confidential IPO papers on 1 June 2026 and its public S-1 on 26 October. Each private round had multiplied the price tag. The IPO now tests whether public investors will pay more than private ones did.

lesson.concept: How a company's IPO price tag is worked out
lesson.big_idea: A company's valuation is its share price times its number of shares. Only the shares sold in the IPO bring in cash. The total also changes depending on which shares you count.

steps.title: A company is cut into shares
steps.text: A share is a small slice of ownership. If a company has 1,000 shares and you own one, you own one-thousandth of the company.

steps.title: Price times shares gives valuation
steps.text: Valuation, also called market capitalisation, is one share's price multiplied by the number of shares. Anthropic's range is $70 to $78 a share. A higher share price raises the whole total.

steps.title: Cash raised is much smaller
steps.text: An IPO sells only some of the shares. Money raised is shares sold times price. Anthropic offers 825 million shares. At $78 each, that is $64.35 billion, far below its valuation.

steps.title: Which shares you count matters
steps.text: Staff stock options and convertible instruments (loans or notes that can turn into shares) may add shares later. Counting them gives a bigger 'fully diluted' total. NBC says the $1.4 trillion figure appears to be measured this way.

steps.title: Compare with the last price
steps.text: Investors compare an IPO valuation with the last private price. Private investors valued Anthropic at $965 billion in May 2026. The IPO tests whether public buyers will pay more.

example.setup: Say a startup has 1,000 shares after its IPO. It has also made promises, through options and convertibles, that could become 400 more shares. In the IPO it sells 100 shares at ₹100 each.

lines.note: Only the shares actually sold bring in money.

lines.label: Basic valuation
lines.note: Every existing share is priced at the IPO price.

lines.label: Fully diluted shares
lines.note: Add the shares promised through options and convertibles.

lines.label: Fully diluted valuation
lines.note: Same price, more shares, so a bigger total.

lines.label: The gap
lines.note: Nothing about the business changed. Only the share count did.

example.result: At the same price, the same company has two price tags: ₹1 lakh or ₹1.4 lakh. The cash it actually raises, ₹10,000, is only one-tenth of even the smaller figure.

apply.text: Anthropic's numbers work the same way. Selling 825 million shares at up to $78 raises up to $64.35 billion. NBC says the range implies about $1.02 trillion, and the $1.4 trillion figure appears to be fully diluted. That looks like the gap in our example, but no source has fully reconciled the two. Either way, the cash raised is a small share of the price tag.

practice.q: Suppose Anthropic prices its shares at the bottom of its range, $70. How much would the IPO itself raise?
practice.answer: Cash raised = shares sold × price. 825 million × $70 = 57,750 million dollars, or $57.75 billion. That is $6.6 billion less than the $64.35 billion it would raise at $78.

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi talks move on prisoners, not on land or ceasefire
stories.question: Did the Abu Dhabi talks bring Russia and Ukraine any closer to ending the war?
stories.dek: Only a little. Day one on 10 November moved towards a large prisoner swap. The core fights over land and a ceasefire are still unsolved, and the US expects no quick fix.

so_far.text: The US has hosted three-way Russia–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi before. Rounds on 23–24 January and 4–5 February 2026 produced no ceasefire. Their only result was a 314-prisoner swap. No three-way meeting followed until November. By mid-October 2026, reports said Ukraine was nearly or fully out of Patriot air-defence missiles. Going into the new round, US officials said they wanted a 'final end' to the war.

what_happened.text: US-mediated Russia–Ukraine talks opened in Abu Dhabi on 10 November 2026, the first three-way meeting since February. The first session lasted nearly four hours. Ukraine's leader, Zelensky, called it 'constructive and quite substantive'. It focused on humanitarian issues: prisoner exchanges, captive civilians and children taken from Ukraine. He said a swap of '1,000 for 1,000' or '1,500 for 1,500' was discussed, with no date set. Russia raised territory; Zelensky said only leaders can settle it. Day two, on 11 November, was to cover de-escalation, energy, the Black Sea and a possible leaders' meeting. Its outcome was not yet reported.

steps.text: Russia wants one comprehensive deal covering land, NATO and limits on Ukraine's army, so it rejects a general halt in fighting.
Ukraine wants an immediate ceasefire first and refuses to give up land or accept limits on its military.
Each side's first step is the other side's last, so day one moved to humanitarian issues like prisoner swaps.
Territory is pushed up to leaders, but Putin has rejected meeting Zelensky, so the core dispute has nowhere to go.
The US is widening the talks to Russia–Europe security, but Russia keeps Europeans away from this table for now.

history.text:
The dispute is rooted in land. In September 2022 Russia declared it had annexed four Ukrainian regions, even though its army did not fully control them. That claim still shapes every round of talks. Russia wants Ukraine out of all four regions. Ukraine refuses to give up territory.

On 21 November 2025, US sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil, two big Russian oil firms, took effect. Indian refiners cut back on Russian crude as a result.

In 2026 the US brought both sides to Abu Dhabi. Rounds on 23–24 January and 4–5 February produced no ceasefire. The only result was a swap of 314 prisoners, 157 on each side, on 5 February. It was the first swap in five months. Russia demanded that Ukraine leave the roughly 20% of Donetsk province it still held. Ukraine said no. Zelensky also said Western allies would send troops after a ceasefire, with US backing if Russia kept breaking it. Russia has repeatedly rejected any Western troops in Ukraine.

No three-way meeting took place again until November. Meanwhile, by mid-October 2026, reports said Ukraine was nearly or fully out of Patriot interceptors. These are missiles that shoot down incoming missiles. Reports tie the shortage largely to the US–Iran war. This was the situation when the new round began.

lesson.concept: Why the order of steps can stall peace talks
lesson.big_idea: In peace talks, each side often wants its own priority settled first. When one side's first step is the other side's last step, talks stall, and mediators turn to small deals that build trust.

steps.title: A ceasefire is not peace
steps.text: A ceasefire only stops the shooting. It settles nothing else. A peace settlement decides the hard questions: borders, alliances and the size of armies. The two can come in either order.

steps.title: Each side picks an order
steps.text: Ukraine wants an immediate ceasefire first, then talks. Russia wants one comprehensive deal first, on land, NATO and limits on Ukraine's army, and rejects a general halt in fighting.

steps.title: Why order is leverage
steps.text: Leverage means the pressure you can put on the other side. Fighting while talking keeps that pressure on. A pause removes it. So the side that wants a deal first resists a ceasefire, and the other side resists the opposite.

steps.title: Small deals build a path
steps.text: When the order cannot be agreed, mediators look for steps both sides gain from, like prisoner swaps. These help families and build some trust. They do not settle the core dispute.

steps.title: The top question goes to leaders
steps.text: The hardest question, land, is often left for leaders to settle. If one leader refuses to meet, that question has nowhere to go. Putin has rejected meeting Zelensky.

example.setup: Imagine two sides, Red and Blue, fighting over a strip of land. Red holds most of it. Blue wants the shooting to stop first; Red wants the land settled first.

lines.label: Blue's offer
lines.calc: Ceasefire first, then talk about land
lines.note: Stops Blue's losses while talking.

lines.label: Red's reply
lines.calc: Settle land first, then stop shooting
lines.note: Keeps military pressure on Blue while talking.

lines.label: The deadlock
lines.calc: Each side's first step is the other's last
lines.note: Neither can say yes without giving up its leverage.

lines.label: The workaround
lines.note: Both sides gain; the land question is untouched.

lines.label: Send it upstairs
lines.note: Works only if both leaders agree to meet.

example.result: Talks can make real humanitarian progress and still not bring the war closer to ending, because the order of steps is itself the dispute.

apply.text: That is what Abu Dhabi showed on 10 November. Ukraine wants a ceasefire first; Russia wants a full deal and rejects a halt. So day one moved on a 1,000-for-1,000 or 1,500-for-1,500 prisoner swap. Territory was pushed to leaders, and Putin has rejected meeting Zelensky.

practice.q: Suppose Red offers a 30-day ceasefire, but only after Blue agrees to hand over half the disputed land. Has the deadlock broken?
practice.answer: Step 1: Red's offer still puts land first; the ceasefire comes only after Blue gives land. Step 2: Blue's rule is ceasefire first and no land given. Step 3: so Blue's first step is still not Red's first step. The order has not changed, so the deadlock holds.

scenes.say: 10 November ko Russia aur Ukraine phir se Abu Dhabi mein baithe, aur beech mein tha United States. Kya in talks se jung khatam hone ke kareeb aayi? Bas thoda sa. Chaliye samajhte hain kyun.
scenes.speak: 10 November को Russia और Ukraine फिर से Abu Dhabi में बैठे, और बीच में था United States। क्या इन talks से जंग ख़त्म होने के क़रीब आई? बस थोड़ा सा। चलिए समझते हैं क्यों।

scenes.say: February ke baad yeh pehli three way meeting thi, aur lagbhag 4 ghante chali. Ukraine ke leader Zelensky ne ise constructive aur kaafi substantive bataya. Zyadatar baat humanitarian muddon par hui: prisoner exchange, qaid civilians, aur Ukraine se le jaaye gaye bachche.
scenes.speak: February के बाद यह पहली three way meeting थी, और लगभग 4 घंटे चली। Ukraine के leader Zelensky ने इसे constructive और काफ़ी substantive बताया। ज़्यादातर बात humanitarian मुद्दों पर हुई: prisoner exchange, क़ैद civilians, और Ukraine से ले जाए गए बच्चे।

scenes.say: Zelensky ne kaha ek bade swap par baat hui: 1000 ke badle 1000, ya 1500 ke badle 1500. Koi date announce nahi hui. Russia ne territory ka mudda uthaya, lekin Zelensky bole ki yeh sirf leaders tay kar sakte hain. Day two, yaani 11 November, ke results tab tak saamne nahi aaye the.
scenes.speak: Zelensky ने कहा एक बड़े swap पर बात हुई: 1000 के बदले 1000, या 1500 के बदले 1500। कोई date announce नहीं हुई। Russia ने territory का मुद्दा उठाया, लेकिन Zelensky बोले कि यह सिर्फ़ leaders तय कर सकते हैं। Day two, यानी 11 November, के results तब तक सामने नहीं आए थे।

scenes.say: Zameen sab kuch kyun rok deti hai, yeh samajhne ke liye chaliye September 2022 mein. Russia ne elaan kiya ki usne Ukraine ke 4 regions annex kar liye, jabki uski army ka un par poora control nahi tha. Russia ab bhi chahta hai ki Ukraine chaaron se nikal jaaye. Ukraine zameen chhodne se mana karta hai.
scenes.speak: ज़मीन सब कुछ क्यों रोक देती है, यह समझने के लिए चलिए September 2022 में। Russia ने ऐलान किया कि उसने Ukraine के 4 regions annex कर लिए, जबकि उसकी army का उन पर पूरा control नहीं था। Russia अब भी चाहता है कि Ukraine चारों से निकल जाए। Ukraine ज़मीन छोड़ने से मना करता है।

scenes.say: Ab turning points. November 2025 mein Russian oil companies Rosneft aur Lukoil par US sanctions lagu hue. 2026 ki shuruaat mein Abu Dhabi mein 2 round hue, lekin ceasefire nahi mila. Result bas itna: 314 prisoners swap hue, har taraf se 157.
scenes.speak: अब turning points। November 2025 में Russian oil companies Rosneft और Lukoil पर US sanctions लागू हुए। 2026 की शुरुआत में Abu Dhabi में 2 round हुए, लेकिन ceasefire नहीं मिला। Result बस इतना: 314 prisoners swap हुए, हर तरफ़ से 157।

scenes.say: Russia ne yeh bhi maanga ki Ukraine Donetsk ka woh lagbhag 20 percent hissa chhod de jo uske paas bacha tha. Ukraine ne mana kar diya. Phir November tak koi three way talks nahi. Isi beech, mid October tak reports aayi ki Ukraine ke Patriot interceptors lagbhag khatam ho chuke the. Yeh woh missiles hain jo aati hui missiles ko rokti hain. Badi wajah thi US aur Iran ki jung.
scenes.speak: Russia ने यह भी माँगा कि Ukraine Donetsk का वो लगभग 20 percent हिस्सा छोड़ दे जो उसके पास बचा था। Ukraine ने मना कर दिया। फिर November तक कोई three way talks नहीं। इसी बीच, mid October तक reports आईं कि Ukraine के Patriot interceptors लगभग ख़त्म हो चुके थे। ये वो missiles हैं जो आती हुई missiles को रोकती हैं। बड़ी वजह थी US और Iran की जंग।

scenes.say: Toh deal itni mushkil kyun hai? Ek: Russia zameen, NATO aur Ukraine ki army par limits, sab par ek poori deal chahta hai, aur fighting mein general rok ko reject karta hai. Do: Ukraine pehle ceasefire chahta hai, aur na zameen dega, na apni army limit karega.
scenes.show: Full deal first vs ceasefire first
scenes.speak: तो deal इतनी मुश्किल क्यों है? एक: Russia ज़मीन, NATO और Ukraine की army पर limits, सब पर एक पूरी deal चाहता है, और fighting में general रोक को reject करता है। दो: Ukraine पहले ceasefire चाहता है, और न ज़मीन देगा, न अपनी army limit करेगा।

scenes.say: Teen: ek side ka pehla kadam doosri side ka aakhri kadam hai, isliye negotiators woh cheezein dhoondhte hain jo dono maan sakein, jaise prisoner swaps. Chaar: zameen ka mudda leaders tak jaata hai, lekin Putin Zelensky se milne se mana kar chuke hain. Paanch: US, Russia aur Europe ke beech ek badi security deal chahta hai.
scenes.speak: तीन: एक side का पहला कदम दूसरी side का आख़िरी कदम है, इसलिए negotiators वो चीज़ें ढूँढते हैं जो दोनों मान सकें, जैसे prisoner swaps। चार: ज़मीन का मुद्दा leaders तक जाता है, लेकिन Putin Zelensky से मिलने से मना कर चुके हैं। पाँच: US, Russia और Europe के बीच एक बड़ी security deal चाहता है।

scenes.say: Kamre mein kaun tha? Russia ko lead kiya Vladimir Medinsky ne, saath mein deputy foreign ministers aur military intelligence chief. Ukraine ko lead kiya Rustem Umerov ne. US ki taraf se Steve Witkoff aur Jared Kushner mediator the, aur US jung ko poori tarah khatam karna chahta hai. NATO ke ek commander, General Grynkewich, bhi wahan maujood the.
scenes.speak: कमरे में कौन था? Russia को lead किया Vladimir Medinsky ने, साथ में deputy foreign ministers और military intelligence chief। Ukraine को lead किया Rustem Umerov ने। US की तरफ़ से Steve Witkoff और Jared Kushner mediator थे, और US जंग को पूरी तरह ख़त्म करना चाहता है। NATO के एक commander, General Grynkewich, भी वहाँ मौजूद थे।

scenes.say: Europe main table par nahi tha. Ukraine pehle US envoys se mila, Britain, France, Germany, Italy, NATO aur European Commission ke saath. Russia ko table par Europeans se aitraaz tha, lekin usne kaha EU baad mein jud sakta hai. Russia ceasefire ke baad Ukraine mein Western troops ko bhi reject karta hai, jo Zelensky ke mutabik allies bhejenge.
scenes.show: Europe briefed, not at the table
scenes.speak: Europe main table पर नहीं था। Ukraine पहले US envoys से मिला, Britain, France, Germany, Italy, NATO और European Commission के साथ। Russia को table पर Europeans से ऐतराज़ था, लेकिन उसने कहा EU बाद में जुड़ सकता है। Russia ceasefire के बाद Ukraine में Western troops को भी reject करता है, जो Zelensky के मुताबिक़ allies भेजेंगे।

scenes.say: Ab numbers dekhiye. Reports ke mutabik Western Patriot missile deliveries 2023 mein 675 thi, jo 2025 mein gir kar 364 reh gayi. 2026 ke liye 264 planned hain. Zelensky kehte hain ki winter ke liye Ukraine ko 300 se 360 chahiye.
scenes.speak: अब numbers देखिए। Reports के मुताबिक़ Western Patriot missile deliveries 2023 में 675 थीं, जो 2025 में गिर कर 364 रह गईं। 2026 के लिए 264 planned हैं। Zelensky कहते हैं कि winter के लिए Ukraine को 300 से 360 चाहिए।

scenes.say: Talks ke liye jung ruki nahi. Ukraine ki air force ke mutabik, 10 November tak ki raat Russia ne Ukraine par 162 drones aur ek ballistic missile daage. Front line zyadatar deadlock mein hai.
scenes.speak: Talks के लिए जंग रुकी नहीं। Ukraine की air force के मुताबिक़, 10 November तक की रात Russia ने Ukraine पर 162 drones और एक ballistic missile दागे। Front line ज़्यादातर deadlock में है।

scenes.say: Ab swaps ko compare kijiye. February mein: har side se 157. Ab baat ho rahi hai: har side se 1000 ya 1500, yaani lagbhag 10 guna tak bada. Families ke liye yeh asli progress hai, lekin zameen ko yeh chhoota bhi nahi.
scenes.show: Swap: up to ten times bigger
scenes.speak: अब swaps को compare कीजिए। February में: हर side से 157। अब बात हो रही है: हर side से 1000 या 1500, यानी लगभग 10 गुना तक बड़ा। Families के लिए यह असली progress है, लेकिन ज़मीन को यह छूता भी नहीं।

scenes.say: Ab woh idea jo seekhna hai. Peace talks mein steps ka order khud deadlock ban sakta hai. Ceasefire sirf goli chalna rokta hai. Peace deal borders, alliances aur armies tay karti hai. Ukraine pehle ceasefire chahta hai. Russia pehle poori deal chahta hai.
scenes.show: The order of steps is the deadlock
scenes.speak: अब वो idea जो सीखना है। Peace talks में steps का order ख़ुद deadlock बन सकता है। Ceasefire सिर्फ़ गोली चलना रोकता है। Peace deal borders, alliances और armies तय करती है। Ukraine पहले ceasefire चाहता है। Russia पहले पूरी deal चाहता है।

scenes.say: Order itna matter kyun karta hai? Baat karte hue ladte rehne se doosri side par pressure bana rehta hai. Rukne se woh pressure hat jaata hai. Isliye mediators chhoti deals dhoondhte hain jinse dono ko fayda ho, jaise prisoner swaps. Sabse mushkil sawaal, zameen, leaders ke paas jaata hai. Agar ek leader milne ko taiyaar nahi, toh maamla atak jaata hai.
scenes.speak: Order इतना matter क्यों करता है? बात करते हुए लड़ते रहने से दूसरी side पर pressure बना रहता है। रुकने से वो pressure हट जाता है। इसलिए mediators छोटी deals ढूँढते हैं जिनसे दोनों को फ़ायदा हो, जैसे prisoner swaps। सबसे मुश्किल सवाल, ज़मीन, leaders के पास जाता है। अगर एक leader मिलने को तैयार नहीं, तो मामला अटक जाता है।

scenes.say: Maan lijiye Red aur Blue ek zameen par lad rahe hain, jo zyadatar Red ke paas hai. Blue kehta hai: pehle goli band karo, phir zameen ki baat. Red kehta hai: pehle zameen settle karo, phir hum rukenge. Har ek ka pehla kadam doosre ka aakhri hai. Toh woh har side se 100 prisoners swap karte hain aur zameen leaders ko bhej dete hain. Progress hai, lekin peace nahi.
scenes.show: Red vs Blue: who goes first?
scenes.speak: मान लीजिए Red और Blue एक ज़मीन पर लड़ रहे हैं, जो ज़्यादातर Red के पास है। Blue कहता है: पहले गोली बंद करो, फिर ज़मीन की बात। Red कहता है: पहले ज़मीन settle करो, फिर हम रुकेंगे। हर एक का पहला कदम दूसरे का आख़िरी है। तो वो हर side से 100 prisoners swap करते हैं और ज़मीन leaders को भेज देते हैं। Progress है, लेकिन peace नहीं।

scenes.say: Kaun kya keh raha hai? Ukraine: pehle ceasefire, zameen nahi denge. Russia: 4 regions, Ukraine ke liye NATO nahi, ek poori deal, sirf pause nahi. Kushner: ek naya framework, jismein Russia aur Europe seedhe baat karein. Rubio: bahut productive, lekin 24 ghante mein solve nahi hoga. Germany ke Merz: bahut zyada ummeedein mat rakhiye.
scenes.speak: कौन क्या कह रहा है? Ukraine: पहले ceasefire, ज़मीन नहीं देंगे। Russia: 4 regions, Ukraine के लिए NATO नहीं, एक पूरी deal, सिर्फ़ pause नहीं। Kushner: एक नया framework, जिसमें Russia और Europe सीधे बात करें। Rubio: बहुत productive, लेकिन 24 घंटे में solve नहीं होगा। Germany के Merz: बहुत ज़्यादा उम्मीदें मत रखिए।

views.view: Ceasefire first; no land ceded; leaders must settle territory
Four regions, no NATO, army limits, one full deal
New framework; Russia and Europe must talk directly
Very productive, but not solved in next 24 hours

scenes.say: Ek aam galti: yeh sochna ki in talks mein ceasefire par sehmati banni thi. Is round mein aisa nahi tha. Russia fighting mein general rok ko reject karta hai aur ek poori deal chahta hai. Day one ka focus tha prisoners, qaid civilians aur bachche.
scenes.show: Myth: a ceasefire was on offer
scenes.speak: एक आम ग़लती: यह सोचना कि इन talks में ceasefire पर सहमति बननी थी। इस round में ऐसा नहीं था। Russia fighting में general रोक को reject करता है और एक पूरी deal चाहता है। Day one का focus था prisoners, क़ैद civilians और बच्चे।

scenes.say: India mein aapke liye iska kya matlab hai? Seedhe taur par, abhi tak zyada kuch nahi. Kadi hai oil. Rosneft aur Lukoil par US sanctions ke baad Indian refiners ne Russian crude kam kar diya. Trump ne kaha ki India par US tariffs 25 se ghatkar 18 percent ho gaye, aur daava kiya ki India Russian oil kharidna band karne par raazi hai. Delhi ne confirm nahi kiya.
scenes.speak: India में आपके लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? सीधे तौर पर, अभी तक ज़्यादा कुछ नहीं। कड़ी है oil। Rosneft और Lukoil पर US sanctions के बाद Indian refiners ने Russian crude कम कर दिया। Trump ने कहा कि India पर US tariffs 25 से घटकर 18 percent हो गए, और दावा किया कि India Russian oil ख़रीदना बंद करने पर राज़ी है। Delhi ने confirm नहीं किया।

scenes.say: Peace deal se woh sanctions halke honge ya nahi, yeh pata nahi. Aur ab lesson lagaiye: bada prisoner swap asli progress hai. Lekin jab tak steps ke order par jhagda hai, jung khatam hone ke zyada kareeb nahi hai.
scenes.show: Progress on prisoners, not on peace
scenes.speak: Peace deal से वो sanctions हल्के होंगे या नहीं, यह पता नहीं। और अब lesson लगाइए: बड़ा prisoner swap असली progress है। लेकिन जब तक steps के order पर झगड़ा है, जंग ख़त्म होने के ज़्यादा क़रीब नहीं है।

scenes.say: Kya dekhna hai? 11 November ke day two mein kya swap ki date ya leaders ki meeting tay hui? 17 November ko Ramstein group, jo Ukraine ke liye weapons coordinate karta hai, Brussels mein mil raha hai. Abhi bhi pata nahi: agle round ki date aur US plan ki details.
scenes.speak: क्या देखना है? 11 November के day two में क्या swap की date या leaders की meeting तय हुई? 17 November को Ramstein group, जो Ukraine के लिए weapons coordinate करता है, Brussels में मिल रहा है। अभी भी पता नहीं: अगले round की date और US plan की details।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Ek: peace talks mein steps ka order khud deadlock ban sakta hai. Do: Abu Dhabi ek bade prisoner swap ki taraf badha, lekin zameen aur ceasefire abhi bhi unsolved hain. Teen: day two ka nateeja aur 17 November ki Brussels meeting par nazar rakhiye.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। एक: peace talks में steps का order ख़ुद deadlock बन सकता है। दो: Abu Dhabi एक बड़े prisoner swap की तरफ़ बढ़ा, लेकिन ज़मीन और ceasefire अभी भी unsolved हैं। तीन: day two का नतीजा और 17 November की Brussels meeting पर नज़र रखिए।

stories.headline: US orders eye-risk warning on Ozempic and other weight-loss drugs
stories.question: Can weight-loss drugs like Ozempic really cause blindness, and should users worry?
stories.dek: The US now requires a warning about NAION, a rare eye condition that can be permanent. A link to the drugs is possible but not proven. Sudden vision loss still needs prompt care.

so_far.text: GLP-1 drugs copy a gut hormone that helps control blood sugar and appetite. They began as diabetes medicines. Ozempic, made from the ingredient semaglutide, was approved in the US in December 2017. Wegovy, also semaglutide, was approved for weight loss in June 2021. In July 2024 a US study linked semaglutide to NAION, a rare optic nerve disorder. In June 2025 Europe's drug regulator called NAION a very rare side effect of semaglutide. In India, cheap generic semaglutide went on sale on 20 March 2026.

what_happened.text: On 9 November 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) said all GLP-1 drugs must carry a warning about a possible higher risk of NAION. That covers Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Wegovy, Eli Lilly's Mounjaro and Zepbound, and several older diabetes medicines. The warning goes in the label's 'warnings and precautions' section, not a stronger boxed warning. NAION causes sudden, painless vision loss in one eye. It can be permanent and has no known treatment. The FDA found NAION reports for every marketed GLP-1 drug, but its scientists could not identify how the drugs would cause it.

steps.text: When more people take a drug, rare problems that happen to some users get reported more often.
NAION reports turned up for every marketed GLP-1 drug, and studies found higher NAION risk among semaglutide users.
But FDA scientists could not find how these drugs would harm the optic nerve, so cause is not proven.
Regulators warn anyway because NAION can be permanent and has no treatment, so patients must know to act quickly.
The FDA chose a 'warnings and precautions' entry, a step below the boxed warning Australia uses.

history.text:
The story starts in 1988, when scientists discovered the main effects of GLP-1, a gut hormone. Drugs that copy it followed. The US FDA approved Ozempic, made from semaglutide, in December 2017, and Rybelsus in September 2019. In June 2021 Wegovy, also semaglutide, was approved for weight loss. That took the drug beyond diabetes and into weight loss.

The eye question arrived in July 2024. A Mass Eye and Ear study of 16,827 patients, published in JAMA Ophthalmology, found semaglutide users had a higher risk of NAION. Lead author Joseph Rizzo called the results 'significant but tentative'. In June 2025 Europe's drug regulator went further. Its safety committee concluded NAION is a very rare side effect of semaglutide, affecting up to 1 in 10,000 people. Australia's regulator has also put its strongest, boxed warning on all GLP-1 drugs.

India moved on a separate track. Novo Nordisk launched Wegovy in India in June 2025. In March 2026 the Delhi High Court declined to extend patent protection, and the patent expired on 20 March. Cheap generics launched that same day, and Novo Nordisk cut its Indian prices by up to 48% on 31 March. Then, on 9 November 2026, the FDA added its own NAION warning to every GLP-1 drug.

analogy.text: Think of a raffle with one lakh tickets, where about 10 tickets carry a bad prize. Doubling the risk is like adding 10 more bad tickets. That is twice as many, yet almost everyone still draws a blank.
analogy.breaks: Raffle odds are known and fixed. Here the drug's link is unproven, and real risk differs with each person's age and health.

lesson.concept: Relative risk versus absolute risk: what 'doubled' means
lesson.big_idea: A headline saying a drug 'doubles' a risk tells you how many times bigger the risk is, not how big it is. To judge the danger, start from how common the problem already is.

steps.title: Start with the baseline
steps.text: The baseline is how often a problem happens anyway, without the drug. For NAION, the American Academy of Ophthalmology says it affects up to 10 in 1,00,000 (one lakh) people over 50 in the US.

steps.title: Relative risk multiplies it
steps.text: Relative risk says how many times more often a problem appears in drug users. Europe's regulator saw roughly double the risk in type 2 diabetes. A 2024 study found hazard ratios of 4.28 and 7.64.

steps.title: Absolute risk is the real count
steps.text: Absolute risk is the baseline multiplied by the relative risk. The extra cases are the new count minus the baseline. That difference is the added chance one person actually faces.

steps.title: A link is not proof
steps.text: Studies can show users get NAION more often without proving the drug causes it. FDA scientists could not find a mechanism, and the American Academy of Ophthalmology calls the link potential, not established.

example.setup: Imagine 1,00,000 people over 50 taking a GLP-1 drug. Assume NAION would hit 10 of them anyway, and assume the drug doubles that risk.

lines.label: Baseline cases
lines.note: People who would get NAION without the drug.

lines.label: Risk doubled
lines.note: A relative risk of 2 multiplies the baseline.

lines.label: Extra cases
lines.note: Only these could be blamed on the drug, if the link is real.

lines.label: Per person
lines.note: Each user's added chance.

lines.label: Never affected
lines.note: Users who never get NAION at all.

example.result: 'Doubled' sounds frightening, but here it adds about 1 case for every 10,000 users. Small, yet it matters, because NAION can be permanent.

apply.text: So the FDA's 9 November 2026 warning does not mean users are likely to go blind. Europe's regulator puts NAION at up to 1 in 10,000 semaglutide users, a very rare level. But NAION can be permanent and untreatable, so speed matters: see an eye doctor promptly for sudden vision loss, and per Europe's regulator, stop semaglutide if NAION is confirmed.

practice.q: Suppose another study says a drug raises the same rare risk five times, from a baseline of 10 in 1,00,000. How many extra cases, and how many people unaffected?
practice.answer: Baseline: 10 in 1,00,000. Five times: 10 × 5 = 50 in 1,00,000. Extra cases: 50 − 10 = 40 in 1,00,000. Unaffected: 1,00,000 − 50 = 99,950. Even a five-fold rise adds only 4 cases per 10,000 users.

check.q: A drug doubles the risk of a rare eye disease that normally hits 10 in 1,00,000 people. What does that mean?
options: Half of all users will lose their sight
About 20 in 1,00,000 users might get it, instead of 10
Every user's risk rises by 2 per cent
check.why: Relative risk multiplies the baseline: 10 × 2 = 20 in 1,00,000. The extra risk is 10 in 1,00,000, or 1 in 10,000.

takeaways: 'Doubles the risk' is relative; multiply by how common the problem is to see the real risk.

Inmein Novo Nordisk ki Ozempic aur Wegovy, Eli Lilly ki Mounjaro aur Zepbound, aur purani diabetes drugs bhi shaamil hain.

FDA ko har GLP 1 drug ke liye NAION reports mili, lekin drugs ise kaise cause karengi, yeh FDA nahi dhoondh paaya. Warning label ke warnings and precautions section mein jaayegi.

scenes.say: Toh hum yahan tak pahunche kaise? 1988 mein scientists ne GLP 1 ke main effects khoje. Phir uski copy karne wali drugs aayi. Semaglutide se bani Ozempic ko December 2017 mein US mein approval mila. June 2021 mein Wegovy, jo semaglutide hi hai, weight loss ke liye approve hui.

scenes.say: July 2024 mein Mass Eye and Ear ki ek study ne 16827 patients ko dekha, aur semaglutide ko NAION ke zyada risk se joda. Lead author Joseph Rizzo ne ise significant lekin tentative kaha. June 2025 mein Europe ki safety committee ne NAION ko semaglutide ka very rare side effect bataya, 10 hazaar mein 1 tak.
scenes.speak: July 2024 में Mass Eye and Ear की एक study ने 16827 patients को देखा, और semaglutide को NAION के ज़्यादा risk से जोड़ा। Lead author Joseph Rizzo ने इसे significant लेकिन tentative कहा। June 2025 में Europe की safety committee ने NAION को semaglutide का very rare side effect बताया, 10 हज़ार में 1 तक।

scenes.say: India ne apna alag raasta liya. Novo Nordisk ne June 2025 mein yahan Wegovy launch ki. March 2026 mein Delhi High Court ne patent protection badhane se mana kar diya. 20 March ko patent khatam hua, aur usi din saste generics launch ho gaye. 31 March ko Novo Nordisk ne India mein daam 48 percent tak ghata diye.
scenes.speak: India ने अपना अलग रास्ता लिया। Novo Nordisk ने June 2025 में यहाँ Wegovy launch की। March 2026 में Delhi High Court ने patent protection बढ़ाने से मना कर दिया। 20 March को patent ख़त्म हुआ, और उसी दिन सस्ते generics launch हो गए। 31 March को Novo Nordisk ने India में दाम 48 percent तक घटा दिए।

scenes.say: Toh warning ab kyun? Jitne zyada users, utni zyada baar rare problems report hoti hain. Market mein bik rahi har GLP 1 drug ke liye NAION reports aayi. Aur studies mein semaglutide users mein NAION ka zyada risk dikha.
scenes.show: Reports and studies point to a link
scenes.speak: तो warning अब क्यों? जितने ज़्यादा users, उतनी ज़्यादा बार rare problems report होती हैं। Market में बिक रही हर GLP 1 drug के लिए NAION reports आईं। और studies में semaglutide users में NAION का ज़्यादा risk दिखा।

scenes.say: Lekin FDA ke scientists ko koi mechanism nahi mila, isliye cause proven nahi hai. Phir bhi regulators warning de rahe hain, kyunki NAION permanent aur untreatable ho sakta hai, toh patients ko jaldi act karna hoga. FDA ne label warning chuni, jo Australia ki boxed warning se ek step neeche hai. Boxed warning sabse strong hoti hai.
scenes.show: Cause unproven, but damage is permanent
scenes.speak: लेकिन FDA के scientists को कोई mechanism नहीं मिला, इसलिए cause proven नहीं है। फिर भी regulators warning दे रहे हैं, क्योंकि NAION permanent और untreatable हो सकता है, तो patients को जल्दी act करना होगा। FDA ने label warning चुनी, जो Australia की boxed warning से एक step नीचे है। Boxed warning सबसे strong होती है।

scenes.say: Ab players dekhiye. FDA ne warning ka order diya. Novo Nordisk Ozempic, Wegovy aur Rybelsus banati hai. Eli Lilly Mounjaro aur Zepbound banati hai. Europe ki drug safety committee ne 2025 mein action liya. India ke regulator CDSCO ne in drugs ki public advertising par rok laga rakhi hai.

scenes.speak: अब numbers. 2024 की study में hazard ratio, यानी NAION कितने गुना ज़्यादा बार दिखा, diabetes वालों में चार point दो आठ था, और overweight या obesity वालों में सात point छह चार। ये multipliers हैं, chances नहीं।

scenes.say: Pehle yeh dekhiye ki NAION kitna rare hai. American Academy of Ophthalmology kehti hai ki US mein 50 se upar ke har 1 lakh logon mein se 10 tak ko yeh hota hai. Europe semaglutide users ka risk 10 hazaar mein 1 tak maanta hai.
scenes.speak: पहले ये देखिए कि NAION कितना rare है। American Academy of Ophthalmology कहती है कि US में 50 से ऊपर के हर 1 लाख लोगों में से 10 तक को ये होता है। Europe semaglutide users का risk 10 हज़ार में 1 तक मानता है।

scenes.say: Seekhne wali idea hai relative versus absolute risk. Risk double ho gaya, yeh batata hai ki risk kitne guna bada hai, yeh nahi ki kitna bada hai. Step 1: baseline, yaani problem waise bhi kitni baar hoti hai. Step 2: relative risk, yaani users ko yeh kitne guna zyada baar hoti hai. Europe ne type 2 diabetes mein lagbhag double dekha.
scenes.speak: सीखने वाली idea है relative versus absolute risk. Risk double हो गया, ये बताता है कि risk कितने गुना बड़ा है, ये नहीं कि कितना बड़ा है। Step 1: baseline, यानी problem वैसे भी कितनी बार होती है। Step 2: relative risk, यानी users को ये कितने गुना ज़्यादा बार होती है। Europe ने type 2 diabetes में लगभग double देखा।

scenes.say: Step 3: baseline ko relative risk se multiply kijiye. Yahi absolute risk hai, asli ginti. Extra cases matlab yeh ginti minus baseline. Step 4: link proof nahi hai. Ho sakta hai users ko NAION zyada baar ho, bina drug ke cause kiye.
scenes.speak: Step 3: baseline को relative risk से multiply कीजिए। यही absolute risk है, असली गिनती। Extra cases मतलब ये गिनती minus baseline. Step 4: link proof नहीं है। हो सकता है users को NAION ज़्यादा बार हो, बिना drug के cause किए।

scenes.say: Chaliye ek example karte hain. Maan lijiye 50 se upar ke 1 lakh log GLP 1 drug le rahe hain. Maan lo 10 ko NAION waise bhi hota. Double kiya, toh 10 ko 2 se multiply kiya, 20. Extra cases: 20 minus 10, matlab 1 lakh mein 10. Yaani har 10 hazaar users mein 1 extra case.
scenes.speak: चलिए एक example करते हैं। मान लीजिए 50 से ऊपर के 1 लाख लोग GLP 1 drug ले रहे हैं। मान लो 10 को NAION वैसे भी होता। Double किया, तो 10 को 2 से multiply किया, 20. Extra cases: 20 minus 10, मतलब 1 लाख में 10. यानी हर 10 हज़ार users में 1 extra case.

scenes.say: Ek raffle sochiye jismein 1 lakh tickets hain. Lagbhag 10 par bura prize hai. Risk double hone se 10 aur bure tickets jud jaate hain. Do guna, phir bhi 99980 tickets khaali nikalte hain. Lekin raffle ke ulat, yeh link proven nahi hai, aur asli risk har insaan ki umar aur health ke hisaab se alag hota hai.
scenes.speak: एक raffle सोचिए जिसमें 1 लाख tickets हैं। लगभग 10 पर बुरा prize है। Risk double होने से 10 और बुरे tickets जुड़ जाते हैं। दो गुना, फिर भी 99980 tickets ख़ाली निकलते हैं। लेकिन raffle के उलट, ये link proven नहीं है, और असली risk हर इंसान की उम्र और health के हिसाब से अलग होता है।

scenes.say: Kaun kya keh raha hai? Novo Nordisk kehti hai ki data se cause and effect saabit nahi hota. Eli Lilly kehti hai ki notice mein uski drugs ke liye koi specific findings nahi hain. American Academy of Ophthalmology ek potential link dekhti hai, proven cause nahi. Joseph Rizzo ne apne results ko significant lekin tentative kaha.
scenes.speak: कौन क्या कह रहा है? Novo Nordisk कहती है कि data से cause and effect साबित नहीं होता। Eli Lilly कहती है कि notice में उसकी drugs के लिए कोई specific findings नहीं हैं। American Academy of Ophthalmology एक potential link देखती है, proven cause नहीं। Joseph Rizzo ने अपने results को significant लेकिन tentative कहा।

scenes.show: Rare risk, so act fast if it happens
scenes.speak: अब lesson apply कीजिए। Europe risk को 10 हज़ार semaglutide users में 1 तक मानता है, और इसे very rare कहता है। लेकिन NAION permanent हो सकता है, इसलिए speed matter करती है। Europe का regulator कहता है कि NAION confirm हो जाए तो semaglutide बंद कर दीजिए।

Lilly 2026 ke end tak sleep apnoea ke liye Foundayo submit karne ka plan kar rahi hai. Jo pata nahi: kitne Indians yeh drugs lete hain, aur FDA ka exact evidence kya hai.

scenes.speak: आगे क्या? Drug makers final होने से पहले FDA की wording को challenge कर सकते हैं। देखना होगा कि India का regulator US, Europe और Australia के रास्ते चलता है या नहीं। Lilly 2026 के end तक sleep apnoea के लिए Foundayo submit करने का plan कर रही है। जो पता नहीं: कितने Indians ये drugs लेते हैं, और FDA का exact evidence क्या है।

Do: 9 November 2026 ko US ne sabhi GLP 1 drugs par NAION warning ka order diya; link possible hai, proven nahi. stories.headline: Hasina wants to go home; Dhaka wants India to hand her over
stories.question: Will Sheikh Hasina go back to Bangladesh in December, and what does Dhaka want from India?
stories.dek: Not on her own terms for now. Dhaka has refused her a new passport and wants India to extradite her instead. That leaves the decision with New Delhi.

so_far.text: Sheikh Hasina led Bangladesh until 5 August 2024, when a student-led uprising forced her to resign and flee to India. On 17 November 2025 a Bangladeshi court sentenced her to death in absentia over the 2024 crackdown. Her party, the Awami League, is barred from politics. After elections, Tarique Rahman now heads the government. Dhaka's main demand of India is that it stop her political activity from Indian soil. In a Reuters interview published on 10 July 2026, Hasina said she planned to return by December 2026.

what_happened.text: Reports on 9 and 10 November 2026 say Hasina asked Bangladesh for a new passport and a new national ID card so she could return in December. The Bangladesh government refused. It says an active extradition treaty with India already exists, so there is no need for a passport. According to a news agency summary, Bangladesh had earlier cancelled her old passport. Dhaka insists India hand her over through extradition. According to the Times of India, Dhaka called the passport request a political stunt.

steps.text: Bangladesh reportedly cancelled Hasina's passport, so she cannot travel home through normal channels without new papers.
She asked for a new passport and ID card, planning to return in December and surrender to the courts.
She plans to return with other fled Awami League leaders, and Dhaka sees this as a move to rally the party.
So Dhaka refused and points to the 2013 treaty: it wants India to hand her over as a convicted criminal.
That moves the decision to India, which calls extradition a legal issue and says its approach has not changed.

history.text:
Sheikh Hasina has shaped Bangladesh for decades. In her first term as prime minister, from 1996 to 2001, she signed a 30-year Ganges water treaty with India. She returned to power in 2009 and governed for 15 straight years.

In 2013 India and Bangladesh signed an extradition treaty, a deal to send wanted people back to each other. That treaty is now at the centre of the dispute.

In July 2024 a student protest over job quotas grew into an uprising. The crackdown was deadly: the UN says over 1,400 people were killed. On 5 August 2024 Hasina resigned and fled to India, which became her refuge.

On 23 December 2024 Bangladesh formally asked India to extradite her. On 4 April 2025 interim leader Muhammad Yunus asked Modi to stop her 'incendiary statements' from Indian soil.

On 17 November 2025 a special court, the International Crimes Tribunal, sentenced her to death in absentia. That turned the request into a demand to return a convicted person. On 11 August 2026 India said the request was under examination through 'established procedures'.

lesson.concept: How extradition between two countries works
lesson.big_idea: Extradition is when one country formally asks another to send back a wanted person. A treaty sets the rules, but the holding country's courts and government still decide, and political cases can be refused.

steps.title: A treaty sets the rules
steps.text: Two countries sign an extradition treaty, a promise to send back each other's wanted people. India and Bangladesh signed theirs in 2013.

steps.title: The request goes by diplomatic letter
steps.text: The asking country sends a formal request through diplomats, often as a note verbale, an unsigned official letter. Bangladesh sent India one about Hasina on 23 December 2024.

steps.title: The holding country checks it
steps.text: The country holding the person examines the request. Former Indian envoy Pinak Chakravarty says extradition needs a judicial order and legal formalities. India says it is using 'established procedures'.

steps.title: Exceptions can block it
steps.text: Treaties usually let a country refuse in some cases. The 2013 treaty reportedly allows refusal of a request of 'political character', which analysts say leaves India room to decline.

steps.title: The government has the last word
steps.text: Even after the courts, the holding country's government decides whether to send the person. It can say yes, say no, or keep the request under examination.

example.setup: Imagine Country A convicts its former minister, Mr X, while he lives in Country B. The two countries have an extradition treaty. Country A wants him back.

lines.label: Stage 1: the request
lines.calc: A sends B a formal diplomatic note
lines.note: This starts the legal process; nothing moves without it.

lines.label: Stage 2: treaty check
lines.calc: B checks the case is covered by the treaty
lines.note: Some cases fall outside what the treaty covers.

lines.label: Stage 3: the court
lines.calc: A judge in B reviews the evidence
lines.note: A judicial order is needed before any handover.

lines.label: Stage 4: exception test
lines.calc: Is the case of a political character?
lines.note: If yes, B may refuse.

lines.label: Stage 5: the decision
lines.calc: B's government says yes, no, or waits
lines.note: Waiting is also a choice B can make.

example.result: A treaty opens a door but does not force anyone through it. Country B can stall or refuse, so Country A's demand alone cannot bring Mr X home.

apply.text: Bangladesh sent its request on 23 December 2024 and says India has an 'obligatory responsibility' under the treaty. India says only that the request is under examination and is 'a legal issue'. Dhaka has now refused Hasina a passport and insists on extradition instead. In our example's terms, India, the holding country, is still examining the request and has not decided.

practice.q: Suppose Mr Y fled Country A after a bank fraud and had no political role. Country B holds him. Would the political exception likely help him?
practice.answer: Stage 1: Country A sends a formal note. Stage 2: fraud is an ordinary crime, so assume the treaty covers it. Stage 3: a judge checks the evidence. Stage 4: fraud with no political link is unlikely to count as 'political character'. So the exception probably won't help him; it comes down to the evidence and B's government.

stories.headline: Supreme Court says banks should repay scam victims when checks fail
stories.question: Will banks now have to repay Indians who lose money to digital scams?
stories.dek: Not automatically. The Supreme Court wants RBI rules to make banks repay at least the amount lost when the bank's own checks fail. Those rules are not yet in force.

so_far.text: A digital arrest is a scam in which fraudsters pose as officials, such as CBI or ED officers, sometimes with forged court orders. They frighten people into moving money. In September 2025 an elderly couple in Ambala lost about ₹1.05 crore this way. A letter to the Chief Justice led the Supreme Court to take up the issue on its own on 17 October 2025. In late 2025 it asked the CBI to lead a nationwide probe. Separately, the RBI has been preparing new rules on compensating fraud victims.

what_happened.text: On 29 October 2026 a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard the case. Its written order became public around 10 November. The court said the RBI's proposed regulations should require banks to indemnify victims, meaning cover their loss. Banks should pay at least the amount lost where the bank's due diligence failed. This is not an automatic guarantee for every victim. The court also asked WhatsApp and other platforms for anti-scam plans, and discussed an optional WhatsApp 'kill switch' and warnings during long calls.

steps.text: In digital arrest scams, fraudsters posing as officials frighten victims into moving money from their own accounts.
The RBI's 2017 rules give zero liability for outsider breaches, but customers who share credentials bear the loss.
So a victim who sent the money under pressure may find little protection under those rules.
The court says banks can spot unusually large transfers, hold them briefly, alert police and verify in person.
So it wants RBI rules to make banks pay at least the loss when such checks fail.

history.text:
The story starts on 6 July 2017. That day the RBI, which regulates banks, set rules on who bears losses from unauthorised electronic transactions. If an outsider breached an account and the customer reported it within three working days, the customer lost nothing. If the customer's own negligence caused the loss, such as sharing login details, the customer bore it until reporting it. This drew a line: outsiders' break-ins were the bank's problem, and customers' own slips were theirs.

Then digital arrest scams surged. In 2024 cases jumped 465% and losses reached about ₹1,935 crore. In October 2024 Prime Minister Modi publicly warned people about the scam. Many of the gangs are traced to Myanmar, Laos and Cambodia.

In October 2025 a letter about an Ambala couple's ₹1.05 crore loss led the Supreme Court to act on its own. In late 2025 it put the CBI in charge of a nationwide probe, including possible roles of bank staff. The question was no longer only about criminals, but about what banks could have done.

The RBI moved too. In February 2026 it announced compensation of up to ₹25,000 for small-value frauds. Reports in June 2026 said rollout was deferred. Now the court wants more: banks repaying at least the amount lost when their checks fail.

lesson.concept: Who pays when a scam empties your account
lesson.big_idea: When fraud takes money from an account, the rules ask whose fault it was and how fast it was reported. The Supreme Court wants a third question: did the bank do its checks?

steps.title: Start with fault
steps.text: The RBI's 2017 rules first ask who caused the loss. If an outsider broke in (a third-party breach) and you report within three working days, you lose nothing. The bank must credit you within 10 working days.

steps.title: Your own slip shifts the loss
steps.text: If your own negligence caused it, such as sharing your login details, you bear the entire loss until you report it. Reports after seven working days follow the bank's board-approved policy.

steps.title: Why digital arrest slips through
steps.text: In a digital arrest, fraudsters posing as officials frighten you into sending the money yourself. To the bank it can look like your own payment, so the 2017 protections may not help.

steps.title: The new test: bank's checks
steps.text: Due diligence means the reasonable checks a careful bank should make, like pausing an unusually large transfer. The court says if a bank failed them, it should repay at least the amount lost.

example.setup: Say Mr Rao, a retired teacher, normally spends about ₹20,000 a month. Fraudsters posing as CBI officers scare him into sending ₹10 lakh to an unknown account in one go.

lines.label: Who sent it?
lines.note: No hacker broke in, so it looks like his own payment.

lines.label: Old 2017 test
lines.calc: Not a third-party breach, so zero-liability rule may not apply
lines.note: Zero liability is for outsiders breaking in.

lines.label: How unusual?
lines.note: One transfer worth over four years of his usual spending.

lines.label: Bank skipped checks
lines.note: The court's floor: at least the amount lost, if due diligence failed.

lines.label: Bank did check
lines.calc: Held it, called him, alerted police: no automatic payout
lines.note: Compensation is not a guarantee for every victim.

example.result: The same ₹10 lakh loss can end very differently. Under the court's approach, what matters is whether the bank spotted a transfer worth 50 months of normal spending and acted.

apply.text: That is why, at its 29 October 2026 hearing, the Supreme Court said the RBI's proposed rules must carry a liability clause, or it would enforce one by order. Mr Rao's bank would owe ₹10 lakh only if it ignored the warning signs. Until the RBI notifies its rules, this is a principle, not binding law.

practice.q: Suppose a hacker steals Priya's card details and takes ₹40,000. She tells her bank two working days later. How much does she lose?
practice.answer: Step 1: an outsider broke in, so it is a third-party breach. Step 2: she reported within three working days. Step 3: under the 2017 rules her liability is zero. So she loses ₹0, and the bank must credit ₹40,000 within 10 working days.

options: Always, for every scam loss
When the bank failed its checks, such as ignoring an unusually large transfer

check.why: The court tied compensation to a proven failure of the bank's due diligence; it is not automatic for every victim.

takeaways: Who pays for fraud depends on fault, reporting speed and, now, whether the bank did its checks.
The Supreme Court says banks should repay at least the loss when their due diligence fails.
Watch the 23 November hearing and whether the RBI notifies its rules by 30 November.

stories.headline: Fossil emissions dip slightly in 2026, but record heat still looms
stories.question: Fossil-fuel emissions fell in 2026, so why are scientists still warning about record heat?
stories.dek: Fossil CO2 is projected to fall only about 0.4% in 2026, after an energy price shock. But CO2 keeps piling up in the air, and a record El Niño makes 2027 a likely record year.

so_far.text: COP31, the UN climate summit, runs from 9 to 20 November 2026 in Antalya, Turkey. Going in, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) said the chance of holding warming to 1.5°C with no or limited overshoot is gone. Its best path now peaks at 1.7–1.8°C, and current pledges point to about 2.6°C by 2100. In September, Carbon Brief estimated that fossil CO2 might fall about 0.5% in 2026. The International Energy Agency (IEA) expected 2026 oil demand about 2.4% below 2025 after disruption at the Strait of Hormuz.

what_happened.text: On 9 November 2026, COP31's first day, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said 2026 is on course to be one of the four warmest years on record. January–September averaged 1.47°C above 1850–1900, against 1.55°C in record-hot 2024. Sea level hit a record in 2026. The WMO said El Niño is expected to be the strongest on record by December. In findings reported on 10 November, the Global Carbon Project projected that fossil-fuel CO2 will fall about 0.4% in 2026. Its authors warn that talk of a global turnaround is premature.

steps.text: The Iran war caused a short-term energy shock: oil and gas prices soared, pushing people to look beyond fossil fuels.
Coal demand rose 1.2%, but falls in oil and gas more than offset it, so fossil CO2 dipped about 0.4%.
CO2 builds up in the air: it is now 427.7 ppm, 54% above pre-industrial, so a small cut still adds.
Land-use emissions are expected to rise to 5.1 billion tonnes in 2026, mainly from peat fires and El Niño-linked wildfire risk.
El Niño releases heat stored in the ocean, and its biggest effect usually comes the next year, so 2027 may set records.

history.text:
The story starts in 2001, when scientists set up the Global Carbon Project to track the world's carbon. Its Global Carbon Budget began in 2005. From 2013 it became a yearly report with openly updated data. That yearly count is the one now in the news.

In December 2015, countries adopted the Paris Agreement. It aims to keep warming well below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C. Each country sets its own five-yearly plan, called an NDC.

In September 2023, the first global stocktake, an official progress check, found projected warming had fallen from 3.7–4.8°C (the 2010 outlook) to 2.4–2.6°C. But it said emissions had to peak by 2025 to keep 1.5°C in reach.

Then the 2023–24 El Niño peaked in December 2023. It helped make 2024 the hottest year on record and the first calendar year above 1.5°C.

Emissions kept climbing. In November 2025, at COP30, the Global Carbon Budget projected a record 38.1 billion tonnes of fossil CO2. In May 2026, the WMO gave an 86% chance that a year in 2026–2030 beats 2024, and said El Niño makes 2027 a likely record. So 2026's small fall arrives right after a record high, with more heat already lined up.

lesson.concept: Why a small emissions cut doesn't stop warming
lesson.big_idea: Global warming depends on the total CO2 piled up in the air, not on one year's emissions. A small yearly cut still adds to the pile, and El Niño adds short bursts of heat on top.

steps.title: Warming tracks the total
steps.text: Carbon dioxide (CO2) stays in the air for centuries. So warming depends on how much has piled up, not on one year's emissions. The air now holds 427.7 ppm, 54% above pre-industrial levels.

steps.title: A smaller addition still adds
steps.text: When yearly emissions fall slightly, the pile still grows, just a little slower. The projected 0.4% fall in 2026 comes right after a record 38.1 billion tonnes in 2025.

steps.title: The budget is the room left
steps.text: A carbon budget is the total CO2 the world can still emit for a temperature limit. For 1.5°C it is 150 billion tonnes, under four years at current rates.

steps.title: Natural swings ride on top
steps.text: El Niño, a warming of the tropical Pacific, releases heat already stored in the ocean. It pushes single years higher, usually most in the year after it peaks.

example.setup: Suppose the world has 150 billion tonnes of CO2 left in its 1.5°C budget. Assume it emits 40 billion tonnes a year, then trims that by 0.5%.

lines.label: Year 1
lines.note: The budget shrinks by the whole year's emissions.

lines.label: A 0.5% cut
lines.note: A small fall, similar in size to 2026's.

lines.label: Year 2
lines.note: Still shrinking almost as fast as before.

lines.label: Years 3 and 4
lines.note: Without the cut, it also runs out in year 4.

example.result: A small cut only trims each year's addition. The budget still runs out in year four, the same as without the cut. Only emissions near zero stop the pile growing.

apply.text: The Global Carbon Project's 0.4% fall is like the small cut in our example. The world still added close to a record amount of CO2, and the 150-billion-tonne budget keeps shrinking. On top of that, El Niño, expected at record strength by December, usually hits hardest the next year. So the WMO sees 2027 as a likely record.

practice.q: Same 150-billion-tonne budget and 40 a year. Suppose emissions fall 10% instead of 0.5%. How much is left after two years?
practice.answer: Year 1: 150 − 40 = 110 left. A 10% cut: 10% of 40 = 4, so year 2 emits 36. Year 2: 110 − 36 = 74 left. Even a big cut leaves more than half the budget used in two years.

scenes.say: Ab numbers dekhiye. China, jiska fossil emissions mein 32 percent hissa hai, zero point nau percent neeche hai. US, ek point teen neeche. Baaki duniya, zero point saat neeche. India alag hai, chaar point chaar upar. Kul milakar, zero point chaar neeche.
scenes.speak: अब numbers देखिए। China, जिसका fossil emissions में 32 percent हिस्सा है, zero point नौ percent नीचे है। US, एक point तीन नीचे। बाकी दुनिया, zero point सात नीचे। India अलग है, चार point चार ऊपर। कुल मिलाकर, zero point चार नीचे।

scenes.say: Sabse zaroori number: ek point paanch degree par rehne ke liye duniya ke paas lagbhag 150 billion tonne carbon dioxide emit karne ki jagah bachi hai. Current rate par, yeh chaar saal se bhi kam hai.
scenes.speak: सबसे ज़रूरी number: एक point पाँच degree पर रहने के लिए दुनिया के पास लगभग 150 billion tonne carbon dioxide emit करने की जगह बची है। Current rate पर, यह चार साल से भी कम है।

scenes.say: Yeh baat yaad rakhiye. Warming har saal ki matra se nahi, hawa mein kul carbon dioxide se tay hoti hai. Yeh sadiyon tak wahan tikta hai, isliye har saal ka emission dher mein judta jaata hai. Chhota addition bhi addition hi hai. Toh emissions girne ka matlab cooling nahi hai.
scenes.show: Warming follows the total, not one year
scenes.speak: यह बात याद रखिए। Warming हर साल की मात्रा से नहीं, हवा में कुल carbon dioxide से तय होती है। यह सदियों तक वहाँ टिकता है, इसलिए हर साल का emission ढेर में जुड़ता जाता है। छोटा addition भी addition ही है। तो emissions गिरने का मतलब cooling नहीं है।

scenes.say: Ek bathtub sochiye jiska drain lagbhag band hai. Fossil fuels nal hain. Nal thoda dheema kijiye, paani phir bhi badhta hai. Carbon budget woh jagah hai jo overflow se pehle bachi hai. Lekin bathtub mein El Nino nahi hota: ocean jama garmi jhatkon mein chhodta hai.
scenes.speak: एक bathtub सोचिए जिसका drain लगभग बंद है। Fossil fuels नल हैं। नल थोड़ा धीमा कीजिए, पानी फिर भी बढ़ता है। Carbon budget वह जगह है जो overflow से पहले बची है। लेकिन bathtub में El Nino नहीं होता: ocean जमा गर्मी झटकों में छोड़ता है।

scenes.say: Ab hisaab lagate hain. Maan lijiye 150 billion tonne bache hain, aur duniya har saal 40 emit karti hai. Pehla saal: 150 minus 40, bache 110. Ab emissions aadha percent kam kijiye. 40 ka aadha percent hai zero point do, toh emissions ho gaye untalees point aath.
scenes.speak: अब हिसाब लगाते हैं। मान लीजिए 150 billion tonne बचे हैं, और दुनिया हर साल 40 emit करती है। पहला साल: 150 minus 40, बचे 110. अब emissions आधा percent कम कीजिए। 40 का आधा percent है zero point दो, तो emissions हो गए उनतालीस point आठ।

scenes.say: Doosra saal: 110 minus untalees point aath, bache sattar point do. Teesre saal bachte hain tees point chaar. Chauthe saal budget khatam, bilkul waise hi jaise cut ke bina hota. Yahi hai 2026: chhoti si dip, lekin budget sikudta ja raha hai.
scenes.show: Still runs out in year four
scenes.speak: दूसरा साल: 110 minus उनतालीस point आठ, बचे सत्तर point दो। तीसरे साल बचते हैं तीस point चार। चौथे साल budget ख़त्म, बिल्कुल वैसे ही जैसे cut के बिना होता। यही है 2026: छोटी सी dip, लेकिन budget सिकुड़ता जा रहा है।

scenes.say: India ke liye iska kya matlab hai? 2026 mein India ke fossil emissions chaar point chaar percent badhne wale hain. October mein India Meteorological Department ne kaha ki El Nino 2026 ke end tak mazboot hota jaayega, jisse post monsoon season zyaadatar sookha rahega. Reports ke mutabik sardi bhi zyada garam rehne ki ummeed hai.
scenes.speak: India के लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? 2026 में India के fossil emissions चार point चार percent बढ़ने वाले हैं। October में India Meteorological Department ने कहा कि El Nino 2026 के end तक मज़बूत होता जाएगा, जिससे post monsoon season ज़्यादातर सूखा रहेगा। Reports के मुताबिक सर्दी भी ज़्यादा गरम रहने की उम्मीद है।

scenes.say: Kis par nazar rakhein? COP31 20 November ko khatam hoga. El Nino ke December tak record strength par peak karne aur 2027 ki shuruaat tak chalne ki ummeed hai. 2026 ki final climate report March 2027 mein aani hai. Abhi pata nahi: dip ka kitna hissa war ke price spike se aaya, aur India ka 2027 monsoon kaisa hoga.
scenes.speak: किस पर नज़र रखें? COP31 20 November को ख़त्म होगा। El Nino के December तक record strength पर peak करने और 2027 की शुरुआत तक चलने की उम्मीद है। 2026 की final climate report March 2027 में आनी है। अभी पता नहीं: dip का कितना हिस्सा war के price spike से आया, और India का 2027 monsoon कैसा होगा।

stories.headline: Rubio says economic pressure, not more combat, will squeeze Iran
stories.question: Is the US-Iran war winding down even as Iran's threats spread to Europe?
stories.dek: Partly. Washington says economic pressure, not bombs, will now do the work, and oil fell below $90. But no deal is signed, ships were hit on 8 November, and France blames Iran for cyberattacks.

so_far.text: The US–Iran war began on 28 February 2026, when the US and Israel struck Iran and killed Supreme Leader Khamenei. Iran retaliated and blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil shipping lane. A spring ceasefire and a June deal both collapsed, and fighting resumed from September. On 8 November Trump said new strikes were 'highly unlikely' if Iran signs a strong deal.

what_happened.text: On 10 November, after G7 foreign ministers met in Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said further major combat against Iran is no longer needed, because US economic pressure is doing enough damage to Tehran's leadership. Brent crude briefly fell below $90 a barrel, the first time since August. On 9 November, France accused Iran's Revolutionary Guard of cyberattacks on fridges at over 700 French shops, causing losses of tens of millions of euros. The same day, the US moved at least eight tanker planes out of RAF Mildenhall in Britain after a reported Iranian threat.

steps.text: The US blockade and sanctions squeeze Iran's income; Rubio says this already damages Tehran's leadership enough.
So big bombing raids look unnecessary to Washington; Trump says new strikes are 'highly unlikely' if Iran signs a strong deal.
Traders read fewer strikes as less risk to Gulf oil, so Brent dipped below $90 on 10 November.
Pressure appears elsewhere: France blames Iran for cyberattacks, and the US moved aircraft after a reported Iranian threat in Britain.
With no signed deal, ships near Hormuz were still hit on 7–8 November, so the war is quieter, not over.

history.text: In 1953 a US- and UK-backed coup removed Iran's prime minister, Mosaddegh, after he nationalised oil. The 1979 Islamic Revolution then broke relations with the US. In 2018 the Trump administration abandoned the 2015 nuclear deal and reimposed sanctions under 'maximum pressure', the economic tool Rubio now leans on. In June 2025 Israel and the US struck Iranian nuclear sites in the Twelve-Day War, and UN sanctions returned in September. The war began on 28 February 2026. After an April ceasefire, talks in Islamabad failed and the US blockaded Iran by sea. A 17 June memorandum lifted both blockades, but the ceasefire collapsed on 8 July after Iran attacked ships in Hormuz. Fighting resumed from September. Then Europe was drawn in: US bombers left RAF Fairford after a suspected Iran-linked plot, which Iran denies, and France says Iran's Revolutionary Guard hacked its shops in October.

lesson.concept: How war fears get priced into oil
lesson.big_idea: An oil price carries a hidden extra for fear: the chance supply gets cut. When leaders signal fewer strikes, that chance falls, so the price drops even before any deal is signed.

steps.title: Start with a normal price
steps.text: Without war, oil has an everyday price set by supply and demand. Brent began 2026 near $60 a barrel, before the war started on 28 February.

steps.title: Fear adds a risk premium
steps.text: If a key route like the Strait of Hormuz might close, buyers pay extra up front to lock in oil. That extra is the risk premium: a payment for fear of shortage.

steps.title: The premium follows the odds
steps.text: Traders weigh two futures: route open, price low; route shut, price high. The likelier the bad future, the closer the price moves to it. In spring 2026 Brent spiked as high as $130.

steps.title: Words can move the odds
steps.text: Leaders' signals change the odds before anything physical changes. A promise of fewer strikes lowers the chance of a shutdown, so the premium shrinks and the price falls.

steps.title: The price feeds India's bill
steps.text: India buys crude abroad, so the price lands in its import bill. By one rule of thumb, each $1 rise per barrel adds $1.8–2 billion a year.

example.setup: Imagine traders think there is a 50% chance Hormuz stays disrupted. Assume oil would cost $120 a barrel if it does, and $60 if it reopens.

lines.label: Bad future's share
lines.note: Half the weight on a disrupted route

lines.label: Good future's share
lines.note: Half the weight on a reopened route

lines.label: Price before the signal
lines.note: $30 above the $60 calm price: that is the fear premium

lines.label: Odds fall
lines.note: Leaders say new strikes are unlikely

lines.label: New price
lines.note: The fear premium shrinks from $30 to $15

lines.label: India's yearly saving
lines.note: Using the rule of thumb of $1.8–2 billion per $1

example.result: Nothing physical changed in the example, only the odds. Yet the price fell from $90 to $75, and India's yearly import bill would shrink by $27–30 billion.

apply.text: That is the pattern in November 2026. Trump said on 8 November new strikes were 'highly unlikely' with a strong deal, and Rubio said on 10 November major combat was no longer needed. Brent dipped below $90, the first time since August. Some premium remains: Brent is still above its $60 start, ships were hit on 7–8 November, and no deal is confirmed.

practice.q: Same numbers, but a signed deal cuts the chance of disruption to 10%. What is the price, and how much would India save compared with $90?
practice.answer: Bad future: 10% × $120 = $12. Good future: 90% × $60 = $54. Price: $12 + $54 = $66. That is $24 below $90. India saves $24 × $1.8–2 billion = about $43–48 billion a year.

stories.headline: IBM ends US visa sponsorship for most of its consulting roles
stories.question: IBM is stopping visa and green card sponsorship, so what does it mean for Indian tech workers?
stories.dek: IBM will stop backing US work visas and green cards for most IBM Consulting jobs. Affected staff can work for IBM outside the US or leave. Another route to US careers is narrowing.

so_far.text: The H-1B is a US work visa for skilled foreign workers. An employer must sponsor, or formally back, each worker. Many H-1B workers later seek a green card, meaning permanent US residence. The employer usually sponsors that too. Indian IT firms have long been leading H-1B users. By one rough estimate, about 71% of H-1B holders are from India. Since September 2025, US rules on both have tightened.

what_happened.text: On 10 November 2026 IBM said it will stop US visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in IBM Consulting. That is IBM's largest division, with more than 150,000 of its 264,300 workers. Bloomberg reported, per Newsweek, that affected workers can keep working for IBM outside the US or leave at the end of the year. An IBM spokesperson said its use of high-skilled visas had declined for years. Reuters tied the move to wider US scrutiny of visa sponsors.

steps.text: H-1B visas and most work-based green cards need a sponsoring employer; if it stops, the worker's US path stops too.
From 21 September 2025, new H-1B petitions faced a $100,000 fee, up from about $1,500; its status after a June 2026 ruling is unclear.
On 8 October 2026 the Labor Department froze green card paperwork at eight firms, citing federal investigations for Microsoft and Adobe.
IBM says its visa use had fallen for years; Reuters links its decision to this wider US scrutiny.
So affected IBM Consulting staff face a choice: keep working for IBM outside the US, or leave at year end.

history.text: The story starts on 20 November 1990, when the US Immigration Act created the H-1B visa. Its first yearly cap was 65,000. It gave US employers a legal way to hire skilled foreign workers. Over the following decades, Indian outsourcing firms became leading users. More H-1B visas went to India-headquartered companies than to US-headquartered ones. In 2021, half of the top 30 H-1B employers were outsourcing firms. Then things changed. By fiscal 2025, Indian IT firms' H-1B filings had dropped by over 50%, though TCS still sponsored 5,364. On 19 September 2025, Donald Trump signed a proclamation setting a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions from 21 September 2025. Before, an application cost about $1,500. On 8 June 2026 a federal judge reportedly ruled the fee unlawful; its status since is unclear. On 8 October 2026 the Labor Department suspended eight firms, including TCS and Infosys, from PERM, the first step of an employer-backed green card. Each step raised the cost or risk of sponsoring. IBM's move came a month later.

lesson.concept: How US employer sponsorship works, step by step
lesson.big_idea: For most foreign tech workers, the US work visa and the green card both need an employer sponsor. If the employer stops, the path stops, unless another sponsor steps in.

steps.title: The employer files first
steps.text: An H-1B is a temporary US work visa for skilled workers. The worker cannot apply alone; an employer files a petition, called sponsoring. From 21 September 2025, new petitions faced a $100,000 fee, against about $1,500 before. A judge reportedly ruled it unlawful in June 2026; its status since is unclear.

steps.title: The visa is tied to the job
steps.text: The H-1B lets you work only for the sponsor that filed it. If that job ends, you need a new sponsor quickly or must leave the US.

steps.title: The green card needs sponsorship too
steps.text: A green card means permanent US residence. For most workers, the employer starts it with PERM: it shows the Labor Department that no suitable US worker is available.

steps.title: Freeze one step, the path stalls
steps.text: Each step waits for the one before. On 8 October 2026 the Labor Department suspended eight firms from PERM, new and pending cases alike. H-1B status was not suspended.

steps.title: No sponsor, no path
steps.text: If an employer stops sponsoring altogether, as IBM plans for most consulting roles, the worker needs a new sponsor, a job outside the US, or must leave.

practice.answer: Step 1: the suspension covers PERM, not H-1B status, so Arjun keeps working. Step 2: PERM is the first green card step, and no new or pending cases are processed, with no end date set. So his green card path pauses unless another sponsor steps in.

scenes.say: Toh IBM aisa kyun kar raha hai? Basics se shuru karte hain. H-1B aur zyadatar work-based green cards, dono ke liye ek employer ka sponsor karna zaroori hai, yaani worker ko formally back karna. Sponsor ruka, toh worker ka raasta bhi ruk jaata hai.
scenes.speak: तो IBM ऐसा क्यों कर रहा है? Basics से शुरू करते हैं। H-1B और ज़्यादातर work-based green cards, दोनों के लिए एक employer का sponsor करना ज़रूरी है, यानी worker को formally back करना। Sponsor रुका, तो worker का रास्ता भी रुक जाता है।

scenes.say: Uske baad cost aur scrutiny dono badhe: pehle 2025 ki fee, phir October ka freeze. IBM kehta hai ki uska apna visa use saalon se kam ho raha tha. Isliye affected staff ke saamne ab ek choice hai: bahar IBM ke liye kaam karein, ya chhod dein.
scenes.show: Higher cost, more scrutiny, fewer visas
scenes.image: United States Citizenship and Immigration Services
scenes.speak: उसके बाद cost और scrutiny दोनों बढ़े: पहले 2025 की fee, फिर October का freeze। IBM कहता है कि उसका अपना visa use सालों से कम हो रहा था। इसलिए affected staff के सामने अब एक choice है: बाहर IBM के लिए काम करें, या छोड़ दें।

scenes.say: Ab players ki baat. IBM Consulting, jo division yeh change kar raha hai. Keith Sonderling, US Labor Secretary, jo green card freeze ke peeche hain. TCS aur Infosys jaisi Indian IT firms, jo lambe samay se top H-1B users rahi hain. Aur Donald Trump, jinhone fee wali proclamation sign ki.
scenes.speak: अब players की बात। IBM Consulting, जो division यह change कर रहा है। Keith Sonderling, US Labor Secretary, जो green card freeze के पीछे हैं। TCS और Infosys जैसी Indian IT firms, जो लंबे समय से top H-1B users रही हैं। और Donald Trump, जिन्होंने fee वाली proclamation sign की।

scenes.say: Ab numbers dekhiye. Fiscal 2026 mein IBM ke 1611 H-1B petitions approve hue. TCS ne fiscal 2025 mein 5364 sponsor kiye. Saal alag hain, lekin IBM ne ek tihai se bhi kam use kiye.
scenes.show: IBM: a smaller H-1B user than TCS
scenes.speak: अब numbers देखिए। Fiscal 2026 में IBM के 1611 H-1B petitions approve हुए। TCS ने fiscal 2025 में 5364 sponsor किए। साल अलग हैं, लेकिन IBM ने एक तिहाई से भी कम use किए।

scenes.say: Aur fee. September 2025 se har naye H-1B petition par 100000 dollar ki fee thi. Pehle ek application ka kharcha lagbhag 1500 dollar tha. Renewals ismein shaamil nahi the. Reports ke mutabik June 2026 mein ek judge ne fee ko unlawful bataya, aur uske baad se iska status clear nahi hai.
scenes.speak: और fee। September 2025 से हर नए H-1B petition पर 100000 dollar की fee थी। पहले एक application का खर्चा लगभग 1500 dollar था। Renewals इसमें शामिल नहीं थे। Reports के मुताबिक June 2026 में एक judge ने fee को unlawful बताया, और उसके बाद से इसका status clear नहीं है।
